Keep `.env*.example` files in sync with required env vars. ## Project Structure ```text langfuse/ |- web/ # Next.js app (UI + tRPC + public REST) |- worker/ # Queue consumers and background processing |- packages/shared/ # Shared domain, DB, queue contracts, repositories |- ee/ # Enterprise package consumed by web |- generated/ # Generated API clients (do not hand-edit) |- fern/ # API definition sources `- scripts/ # Repo scripts ``` - Dependency direction: - `web` -> `@langfuse/shared`, `@langfuse/ee` - `worker` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/ee` -> `@langfuse/shared` - `@langfuse/shared` -> no imports from `web`, `worker`, or `ee` - Queue payload schemas and queue-name contracts are owned by `packages/shared/src/server/queues.ts`. - High-signal shared entry points: - Domain models: `packages/shared/src/domain/{observations,traces,scores}.ts` - Postgres schema: `packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma` - ClickHouse migrations: `packages/shared/clickhouse/migrations/{clustered,unclustered}/*.sql` - Architecture principles live in `.agents/ARCHITECTURE_PRINCIPLES.md`. ## Core Commands - Install deps: `pnpm install` - Dev all packages: `pnpm run dev` - Dev web only: `pnpm run dev:web` - Dev worker only: `pnpm run dev:worker` - Lint all: `pnpm run lint` - Typecheck all: `pnpm run typecheck` / `pnpm tc` - Run a single test file (vitest filters on the filename argument): - web server tests: `pnpm --filter web run test ` (client tests: `pnpm --filter web run test-client `) - worker: `pnpm --filter worker run test ` - shared: `pnpm --filter @langfuse/shared run test ` - Build check: `pnpm run build:check` - Full build: `pnpm run build` - Worktree bootstrap: `bash scripts/codex/setup.sh` - Worktree maintenance: `bash scripts/codex/maintenance.sh` - Install Playwright Chromium: `pnpm run playwright:install` ## Local Data Inspection - For feature testing and debugging, inspect the local databases directly when it helps you understand the existing test data. # Codex Guidelines for `web`

This file covers package-local guidance for this package.
Use root [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for monorepo-level rules.

## Purpose

- Next.js application with UI, tRPC backend, and public REST API routes.
- Check `web/package.json` for current Next.js, React, and tRPC versions before
  version-sensitive work.
- Primary package for frontend and most request/response surface changes.

## Maintenance Contract

- `AGENTS.md` is a living document.
- Update this file in the same PR when material web-local changes occur:
  - new/renamed web entry points
  - new API route families
  - changed web-specific verification commands
- If the change also affects monorepo workflows or other packages, update root
  `AGENTS.md` too.

## High-Signal Entry Points

- App shell/providers: `src/pages/_app.tsx`
- tRPC context/procedures: `src/server/api/trpc.ts`
- tRPC router registry: `src/server/api/root.ts`
- tRPC routers: `src/server/api/routers/*`, `src/features/*/server/*`
- Public REST API routes: `src/pages/api/public/*`
- Unstable public eval APIs: `src/pages/api/public/unstable/{evaluators,evaluation-rules}/*`
- Feature modules: `src/features/*`
- Reusable UI components: `src/components/*`
- Tests:
  - Server integration tests: `src/__tests__/server/*.servertest.ts`
  - Server unit tests: `src/__tests__/server/unit/*.servertest.ts`
  - Client tests: `src/**/*.clienttest.ts(x)`
  - E2E: `src/__e2e__/*`

## Shared Package Imports

- Prefer `@langfuse/shared` in frontend-safe web code for shared types, zod
  schemas, domain contracts, table definitions, prompt/eval/model-pricing
  helpers, and other cross-runtime utilities.
- Use `@langfuse/shared/src/server` only from server-only web code such as
  `src/server/**`, `src/pages/api/**`, and server tests.
- Use `@langfuse/shared/src/db` only in backend or test code that needs direct
  Prisma access; never route it into client bundles.
- Use narrower subpaths such as `@langfuse/shared/src/env` or
  `@langfuse/shared/encryption` only when that focused surface is the clearest
  dependency.
- See `../packages/shared/AGENTS.md` for the full shared export map and what
  each entrypoint contains.
- For the higher-level platform topology across web, worker, Postgres,
  ClickHouse, Redis, and S3, also read the architecture handbook:
  [langfuse.com/handbook/product-engineering/architecture](https://langfuse.com/handbook/product-engineering/architecture)
  with source markdown in
  `../langfuse-docs/content/handbook/product-engineering/architecture.mdx`
  (GitHub mirror:
  [architecture.mdx](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/blob/4188c1ba453240c90a763a8067ef442d68839323/content/handbook/product-engineering/architecture.mdx#L4)).

## Package-Local Skills

- Shared browser-review workflow for user-visible frontend changes:
  [`../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md)
- Large frontend feature, virtualized-list, local state, and React
  effect-free data-flow architecture:
  [`../.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/frontend-large-feature-architecture/SKILL.md)
- Avoidable React effect audits, refactors, and module migrations:
  [`../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md)
- React composition and component API design:
  [`web/.agents/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/vercel-composition-patterns/SKILL.md)
- React/Next.js performance and rendering best practices:
  [`web/.agents/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md`](.agents/skills/vercel-react-best-practices/SKILL.md)
- PostHog product analytics — when and how to instrument user actions:
  [`../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md)
- Sentry error capture — whether and how an error path should report:
  [`../.agents/skills/sentry-instrumentation/SKILL.md`](../.agents/skills/sentry-instrumentation/SKILL.md)

Read these package-local skills before substantial frontend refactors when the
task involves component composition, reusable component APIs, rendering
performance, virtualized lists, local feature stores, bundle size,
React/Next.js performance patterns, or browser-based signoff of user-visible
changes. If you are about to write a `useEffect` or wire form initial values
from loaded data, read the frontend-large-feature-architecture skill first —
most effects that derive or sync state should not exist. When adding a
meaningful user action (button, handler, form, mutation, feature surface),
read the PostHog instrumentation skill and decide explicitly whether the
action should emit an analytics event. When adding or touching an error path —
a `captureException` or `console.error` call, an error boundary, a `catch`
block, a Worker `onerror`, or a Sentry `beforeSend`/denylist filter — read the
Sentry instrumentation skill first and decide whether it should capture at all
(and, for any suppression change, answer "does this rule hide a real error?").

## Web Conventions

- **Before adding or modifying a chart, dashboard, or chart formatter, read
  `src/features/widgets/chart-library/ARCHITECTURE.md` first** — the charts
  manifesto. It owns the data → preparer → visualiser contract: presentation
  decisions (formatting, colors, axis scale, overload) live in the preparer,
  not the chart components.
- Put net-new feature code under `src/features/<feature>/*`; put broadly reusable
  components under `src/components/*`.
- We use tRPC for full-stack web features; register routers in
  `src/server/api/root.ts`.
- Authentication and RBAC guidance lives in `src/features/rbac/README.md`.
- Entitlements guidance lives in `src/features/entitlements/README.md`.
- Prefer Shadcn/ui primitives from `src/components/ui`; if a missing component
  must be installed, ask the user before doing so.
- When you surface a score in the UI, always show its level
  (trace/observation/session/experiment) with the `<ScoreTag>` component
  (`src/components/score-tag.tsx`) and its global color coding (see the
  ScoreTag Storybook story).
- Tailwind is the default styling layer; use the shared palette and globals in
  `src/styles/globals.css`.
- Do not add `useEffect` by default. Use it only when a component must
  synchronize with a concrete system outside React, such as a subscription,
  browser event listener, observer, timer, or imperative third-party API.
  Before writing an effect, name that external system and its setup/cleanup
  lifecycle. If there is no external system, do not use an effect. In
  particular, do not use effects to derive render state, mirror props or query
  data into local state, react to user actions, or reset state when an ID
  changes. Derive during render, run work in the initiating event handler, use
  query APIs for server state, or mount a keyed child once required data is
  available. Do not evade this rule with `useLayoutEffect`, a custom wrapper
  hook, an ESLint suppression, or disabled dependency checks. Use
  `../.agents/skills/refactor-react-effects/SKILL.md` for effect work.
- In flex layouts, prefer `gap-*` over margin-based `space-x-*`/`space-y-*`.
- Treat `!` Tailwind classes as a smell. Step back and fix the owning layout,
  variant, or primitive before overriding with higher specificity.
- When changing shared UI/table patterns, update sibling variants consistently,
  including default-visible and hidden columns or states.
- For component style variants, prefer `cva` with `VariantProps` and merge
  caller classes through `cn`, following existing `src/components/ui/*`
  components:

  ```tsx
  const cardVariants = cva("rounded-md border", {
    variants: {
      intent: { default: "bg-background", error: "border-destructive" },
    },
    defaultVariants: { intent: "default" },
  });

  type CardProps = React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> &
    VariantProps<typeof cardVariants>;

  const className = cn(cardVariants({ intent }), props.className);
  ```

- When anchoring sticky, fixed, or absolute elements to the viewport, use
  `top-banner-offset`, `pt-banner-offset`, `h-screen-with-banner`, or
  `min-h-screen-with-banner` instead of raw `top-0` so banners do not overlap
  the UI.
- **Z-index / layers — key idea: we are migrating from z-indexes to a layer
  system** (start of a developing design system; extend it, don't work around
  it). **To put something on top of something else, use a layer, not a
  z-index.** The app renders inside `#__next`, isolated into one stacking
  context (`globals.css`), so its z-indexes can't escape; overlays go in layers
  that sit outside it and always win. `LAYER_ORDER` is
  `["panel", "agent", "modal", "popover", "tooltip", "toast"]` — containers declared
  in `_document.tsx`, ordered by that array (later = on top), carrying NO z-index.
  `panel` is for docked side surfaces like Sheet, Drawer, and the table peek;
  `modal` is for true blocking Dialog and AlertDialog surfaces.
  **THE RULE (see `src/components/ui/layer.tsx` JSDoc — source of truth): every
  overlay portals through a layer container; never let a Radix/Vaul `*.Portal`
  fall back to `<body>`.** Radix/Vaul primitives route via their `*.Portal`'s
  `container` (the `ui/*` wrappers do this with `useLayerContainer`); bespoke
  imperatively-positioned content renders via `<Layer name="…">`. z-index stays
  local to a layer or component (1–2 max), never to escape the app — the
  `@repo/no-overlay-zindex` lint rule enforces it.
- **Overlay lifecycle — a dropdown that opens a modal should close first**, not
  linger under it (a lifecycle bug, not z-order — don't fix it by re-ranking
  layers). Radix unmounts a Select/DropdownMenu's content on close, so render the
  Dialog as a SIBLING (trigger inside, dialog outside), as
  `useAddLlmConnectionSelect` in `src/components/ModelParameters/index.tsx` does
  (LFE-10615).
- Never import `prettier/plugins/typescript` in client code — it embeds the
  TypeScript compiler, which the SWC minifier miscompiles (dropped bindings →
  production-only `ReferenceError`; caught by the CI client-bundle scan,
  LFE-10645). Format TypeScript with `parser: "babel-ts"` +
  `prettier/plugins/babel` instead, as the eval-template editor does
  (`src/features/evals/components/code-eval-template-form-body.tsx`).
- Public API routes should use
  `src/features/public-api/server/withMiddlewares.ts`, define strict request and
  response types in `src/features/public-api/types/*`, add server tests, and
  update Fern sources when the contract changes.
- Public eval endpoints should keep the split between reusable `evaluators`
  and ingestion-scoped `evaluation-rules`; do not leak `EvalTemplate` or
  `JobConfiguration` naming into the public contract.
- Keep tests independent; in `src/__tests__/server/**`, prefer scoped cleanup or
  unique test data over global reset helpers.
- Put pure server unit tests that do not need Postgres bootstrap under
  `src/__tests__/server/unit/**` so they skip the shared DB setup hook.
- For small utility functions, prefer Vitest in-source tests when colocated
  coverage is the simplest option, especially when the test needs access to
  private implementation details without widening the module API.
- Do not extract private utility functions into separate files only to make
  them testable. Keep them local unless the user explicitly asks for extraction
  or the utility is meaningfully reused.

## Quick Commands

- Dev: `pnpm --filter web run dev`
- Lint: `pnpm --filter web run lint`
- Lint fix: `pnpm --filter web run lint:fix`
- Typecheck: `pnpm --filter web run typecheck`
- Server tests: `pnpm --filter web run test <args>`
- In-source tests: `pnpm --filter web run test:in-source <args>`
- Client tests: `pnpm --filter web run test-client <args>`
- E2E tests: `pnpm --filter web run test:e2e`
- Agent browser install to the default user-level Playwright cache: `pnpm run playwright:install`
- Build: `pnpm --filter web run build`

## Playbooks

### Add/Change tRPC endpoint

1. Implement router/procedure in `src/server/api/routers/*` or
   `src/features/<feature>/server/*`.
2. Register in `src/server/api/root.ts`.
3. Reuse auth/error patterns from `src/server/api/trpc.ts`.
4. Add/adjust server tests under `src/__tests__/server/*`.

### Add/Change public API endpoint

1. Add route in `src/pages/api/public/*`.
2. Define/update contract types in `src/features/public-api/types/*`.
3. Add/adjust server tests in `src/__tests__/server/*`.
4. If API contract changed, update Fern source (`../fern/apis/**`) and regenerate
   outputs (do not hand-edit `../generated/**`).

### Error handling (tRPC + REST)

1. Throw `BaseError` subclasses (eg `LangfuseNotFoundError`) from handlers and services.
2. Let `BaseError`s bubble up to the tRPC and REST middlewares (eg. don't `try/catch` and rethrow in to `TRPCError` the handler)
3. Extend the `BaseError` or its subclasses in [`packages/shared/src/errors/`](../packages/shared/src/errors/) as needed.

### Add frontend feature

1. Prefer `src/features/<feature>/*` for feature-local code.
2. Put broadly reusable components in `src/components/*`.
3. Keep server logic near feature server folders when possible.
4. For meaningful user actions (buttons, form submits, mode switches), decide
   explicitly whether to instrument them with PostHog. Use
   `../.agents/skills/posthog-instrumentation/SKILL.md`.
5. Review the affected user flow in a real browser with the Playwright MCP
   server before signoff. Use
   `../.agents/skills/frontend-browser-review/SKILL.md`.

### Agent browser loop

1. Start the app with `pnpm run dev:web` unless an existing local server is already running.
2. Install Chromium with `pnpm run playwright:install` if Playwright has not been set up on this machine yet.
3. Use the workspace `playwright` MCP server from `.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, or `.vscode/mcp.json` for browser-driven review of user-visible frontend changes, not just debugging.
4. Exercise the primary changed flow and check the resulting UI state for obvious visual regressions before signoff.
5. Inspect traces and other artifacts under `/tmp/playwright-mcp` when a browser session fails.

## Package-Specific Rules

- Router style is Pages Router-centric; follow existing routing patterns.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -euo pipefail

ensure_env_file() {
  local target_path="$1"
  local fallback_path="$2"

  if [ -f "$target_path" ]; then
    return 0
  fi

  cp "$fallback_path" "$target_path"
}

if ! command -v corepack >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "corepack is required. Use an environment with Node.js 24 support."
  exit 1
fi

corepack enable
corepack prepare pnpm@11.10.0 --activate

ensure_env_file .env .env.dev.example
ensure_env_file .env.test .env.test.example

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  if ! docker image inspect "langfuse-in-app-agent-sandbox:latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "packages/in-app-agent-sandbox-runtime/.local-image-built"
  fi

  pnpm turbo run build:docker-image --filter @repo/in-app-agent-sandbox-runtime --output-logs errors-only
else
  echo "Skipping local in-app agent sandbox image build because Docker is not available."
fi

# Install Chromium into the default user-level Playwright cache so frontend
# browser review works on first bootstrap.
pnpm run playwright:install

# Generate the shared Prisma client explicitly in the current worktree before
# the workspace-wide db:generate task, which may be satisfied by Turbo cache.
pnpm --filter=shared run db:generate

# Prisma client generation is needed for typecheck/build tasks.
pnpm run db:generate

  "transcript": "[00:00] Priya Malhotra: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for carving out time. I'm Priya, AE on the account at Redwood, and with me is Ethan from our SE team and Lina from CS. Who do we have on from BeaconHealth?\\n[00:08] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, CTO. Anika is on as well and Jon from SRE. Hey.\\n[00:11] Anika Patel: Hi all.\\n[00:13] Priya Malhotra: Awesome. Objective today is a focused console walkthrough \u2014 specifically tracing, error analysis, and request logs \u2014 so you can see how we'd debug production flows. We'll leave Q&A and then outline next steps.\\n[00:22] Ethan Zhou: Quick note, I'll show live UI, and also a short demo of request-log export and how we attach top-k traces to failed requests.\\n[00:27] Jon Rivera: Great, we mostly care about root cause \u2014 why a particular generate call spiked latency \u2014 and how much PII could be in logs.\\n[00:32] Priya Malhotra: Perfect. I'll hand to Ethan.\\n[00:34] Ethan Zhou: Cool. Pulling up the Console \u2014 bear with me, sometimes the screen share resizes. Ok so this is the Requests view \u2014 you can filter by model, route, and timeframe.\\n[00:45] [00:45] Ethan Zhou: You see here request IDs on the left, status column, tokens consumed, and a small latency sparkline. We also have a column for \"trace score\" which indicates anomalous internal events.\\n[00:58] Anika Patel: That \"trace score\" \u2014 is that an actual statistical anomaly or heuristics?\\n[01:03] Ethan Zhou: It's heuristics + recent baseline. We run a rolling window of per-route medians and flag deviations beyond configurable thresholds. There is an API to pull raw metrics if you want to plug into your own alerting.\\n[01:15] Marcus Lee: How granular are the traces? We want per-shard, GPU-level timing if possible.\\n[01:20] Ethan Zhou: Good question. Traces are hierarchical. We capture request->model-inference->kernel stages. For Dedicated and Private installs we can surface device-level timings \u2014 e.g., GPU copy, kernel invocation \u2014 but in Hosted we give aggregated node-level times and key stage durations. Sometimes the product name gets scrambled in the transcript \u2014 uh, sorry \u2014 I mean we surface the important spans.\\n[01:39] Jon Rivera: And KV cache hits? Can I see cache hit ratio per request?\\n[01:42] Ethan Zhou: Yes, we annotate spans with KV cache metadata \u2014 hit, miss, partial hit \u2014 and you can filter by that. That shows up in the span details pane.\\n[01:48] [01:48] Ethan Zhou: Example: here is a request that had a 95% token increase and we can see a spike in model-generation span because KV cache was a miss.\\n[01:55] Anika Patel: Hmm, can we mask prompt text? We can't have raw PHI in the console.\\n[02:00] Priya Malhotra: Important point \u2014 we offer PII redaction at ingest and masking in the UI. For Hosted we can redact at collection time per-route; for Private you can enforce no prompt text collection or use customer-side redaction before sending.\\n[02:11] Marcus Lee: What's the retention on request logs by default?\\n[02:14] Lina Ortega: Default retention is 30 days for hosted by tier, but we have enterprise options to increase retention and export to your S3 or your SIEM.\\n[02:22] Marcus Lee: Export \u2014 what's the format?\\n[02:24] Ethan Zhou: Exports are JSONL with per-request metadata + span arrays. We can also stream to your Kinesis or put to S3 with encryption via your KMS.\\n[02:33] Jon Rivera: If we want to run an offline analysis, can we request a subset? Like all 5xxs for a given route in a timeframe?\\n[02:39] Ethan Zhou: Yep. Filters support status codes, route, model, latency thresholds, KV cache tags, any metadata tag. You can export filtered results or run an ad-hoc query in Console and then export.\\n[02:47] [02:47] Marcus Lee: Walk me through a failure example \u2014 we've had a case where latency randomly jumps from 80ms to 3s.\\n[02:53] Ethan Zhou: Sure \u2014 here's an example trace. At 00:00 request enters. The pre-proc span shows 20ms, model-infer shows 2.9s. Looking into the kernel-level annotations we see a GPU memory copy stall and then a fallback to CPU quantized path \u2014 so a model cold-start or memory pressure event. In Dedicated this would be surfaced as device OOM hints.\\n[03:14] Anika Patel: How do you detect fallback to different model variants?\\n[03:18] Ethan Zhou: We attach a \"served-with\" tag to request metadata \u2014 e.g., redwood/llama-2-q8_64 \u2014 and if a fallback occurs we show the fallback chain and reason.\\n[03:26] Marcus Lee: You mentioned canary and fallback policies earlier \u2014 can the console show rollout state?\\n[03:30] Priya Malhotra: Yes, Rollouts view shows percentage traffic, models in the pool, and automatic fallback logs. For example, if latency breaches SLO on a canary, the system can auto-failover to the stable variant and we log that as an event with request IDs.\\n[03:43] Jon Rivera: Ok. On SSO and auditing \u2014 we need per-request audit logs forwarding to Splunk.\\n[03:48] Lina Ortega: We support audit log forwarding, SAML-based SSO, RBAC and granular token-level audit. The audit logs are separate from request logs and are forwarded in real-time.\\n[03:58] Anika Patel: Do audit logs include the prompt?\\n[04:00] Priya Malhotra: By default audit logs include metadata about actions (who pulled export, who changed rollout) but not prompt content unless you enable deeper logging. For compliance we can turn off prompt capture.\\n[04:10] [04:10] Marcus Lee: How about encryption at rest and in transit? We use customer-managed KMS for keys in private deployments.\\n[04:16] Ethan Zhou: In Hosted we manage keys but we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private. All transfers use TLS and S3 exports can be encrypted with your KMS prefix.\\n[04:25] Jon Rivera: Great. Let's talk about sampling \u2014 we can't keep full logs for 100% of traffic.\\n[04:29] Ethan Zhou: Absolutely. We have adaptive sampling policies: deterministic sampling (e.g., 1% of requests), error-triggered sampling (capture all 5xx and 4xx above X ms), and stratified sampling by route. You can configure per-route sampling and we persist the sampling decision in headers for correlation.\\n[04:44] Anika Patel: Does adaptive sampling break debugging of rare errors?\\n[04:47] Ethan Zhou: We recommend error-triggered capture so you always capture a representative set of failures. You can temporarily override sampling for a route during an incident.\\n[04:55] [04:55] Marcus Lee: On the traces, sometimes we have batch requests that fan out \u2014 can I see correlation across sub-requests?\\n[05:00] Ethan Zhou: Yes, we maintain trace parent-child IDs and present them in a flamechart. For batched fan-outs you can collapse or expand spans and view combined latency vs per-subreq.\\n[05:09] Priya Malhotra: Quick note: some transcriptions may show product names slightly off, for instance \"Rudwood\" instead of Redwood \u2014 ignore that, sorry.\\n[05:17] Anika Patel: (laughs) got it.\\n[05:19] [05:19] Jon Rivera: Can we create alerts from the Console based on trace-level conditions?\\n[05:22] Ethan Zhou: Yes, alerting rules can be set on aggregated metrics or on trace conditions like repeated 'GPU copy stall' events, error rate per route, or tail latency percentiles. Alerts can notify Slack, PagerDuty, or webhooks.\\n[05:33] Marcus Lee: Do you keep a mapping between request IDs and downstream tool logs? We use Heka/Fluentd and want to correlate.\\n[05:39] Ethan Zhou: We support correlation IDs \u2014 you can inject your trace-id into request metadata and our export preserves it. We also can push logs to your syslog and provide a mapping table.\\n[05:47] Anika Patel: Let's talk about a real integration scenario: we want an on-call flow where SRE sees the trace, then clicks a CTA to open a PagerDuty incident with pre-populated context.\\n[05:56] Ethan Zhou: That's supported. There's an \"Open Incident\" action that creates a PagerDuty incident with link to the trace and attaches the top 5 traces as JSON. You can also set runbooks or internal notes.\\n[06:05] [06:05] Marcus Lee: Okay would love to see a quick example of exporting error traces to S3.\\n[06:09] Ethan Zhou: I'll trigger a filter for status:5xx, last 2 hours, route: /summarize. Running export... and sending to the configured S3 bucket \u2014 job queued. In this demo I've used a sandbox bucket; for production we'd wire to your account.\\n[06:25] Anika Patel: You said job queued \u2014 how long does it take?\\n[06:28] Ethan Zhou: Depends on volume; for a couple of thousand records typically under a minute. For a large export we chunk and compress.\\n[06:35] Jon Rivera: Any throttling concerns?\\n[06:37] Ethan Zhou: Exports are rate-limited per account, but you can request higher quotas for POC. Also we support incremental exports.\\n[06:44] [06:44] Anika Patel: Can we get the exported payload schema before we wire the consumer?\\n[06:48] Priya Malhotra: Yes \u2014 Ethan will drop a schema doc along with the sample export and a small script to map fields into your ELK.\\n[06:55] Ethan Zhou: On error analysis, Console surfaces top-N stack traces and groups by root cause using a similarity heuristic. It's not perfect \u2014 sometimes semantically different errors are grouped \u2014 but we provide filters to re-cluster.\\n[07:07] Marcus Lee: Similarity heuristic \u2014 is that ML based?\\n[07:10] Ethan Zhou: It's a hybrid: token-based fingerprinting plus some ML features for fuzzy matching. You can tune sensitivity.\\n[07:17] [07:17] Anika Patel: Let's talk about the Optimize recommendations \u2014 this is slightly adjacent but useful.\\n[07:21] Priya Malhotra: Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles by route. The Console surfaces potential token savings and projected cost delta if you switch to q4_0 or to a smaller model variant.\\n[07:33] Marcus Lee: How accurate are those cost projections?\\n[07:35] Ethan Zhou: They use historical per-token distributions, request sizes, and our kernel throughput models. Typically within 5-10% of observed cost after rollout, though will vary with traffic changes.\\n[07:45] Jon Rivera: For an internal POC we'll likely try Dedicated or Private \u2014 will tracing differ?\\n[07:50] Ethan Zhou: In Dedicated and Private you get more granular device-level traces and more control over retention and encryption. The console UI is the same; only the backend telemetry granularity changes.\\n[08:01] Anika Patel: Are there any limitations when using Private in an air-gapped environment?\\n[08:05] Priya Malhotra: In air-gapped on-prem deployments we ship a collector that runs internally and writes to your internal object store. You still get the Console control plane if it's VPC-connected; fully air-gapped installs have a local Console bundle. We can share topology guides.\\n[08:18] [08:18] Marcus Lee: Security: does Eks or GKE integration affect trace collection? We run on GKE.\\n[08:22] Ethan Zhou: We provide a sidecar collector or daemonset that extracts telemetry before it leaves your cluster. For GKE/EKS we have Kubernetes integration docs.\\n[08:30] Anika Patel: If we want to disable prompt capture globally, but enable it for a single route temporarily, is that straightforward?\\n[08:35] Ethan Zhou: Yes \u2014 per-route telemetry flags allow you to override default collection settings. You can also set a time-based override.\\n[08:42] [08:42] Jon Rivera: Let's talk cost implications of verbose tracing \u2014 how much does it add?\\n[08:46] Ethan Zhou: Depends on sampling and retention. Full payload capture at high volume can add storage and egress costs; Optimize will estimate this and suggest sampling or export-only-on-errors patterns.\\n[08:56] Marcus Lee: Any customers using 100% of traces in production?\\n[08:59] Ethan Zhou: Very few. Most use targeted capture plus full capture for important routes.\\n[09:04] [09:04] Anika Patel: Do you anonymize tokens when redacting? Like preserve token counts but mask content?\\n[09:09] Priya Malhotra: We can mask or hash token content while preserving lengths and token boundaries for analysis. Good for privacy-preserving debugging.\\n[09:18] Marcus Lee: About the UI, is there an API to fetch the same traces programmatically? We want to integrate into our incident tooling.\\n[09:23] Ethan Zhou: Absolutely. There's a Request Logs API; you can paginate, supply filters, and get signed URLs for exports.\\n[09:30] [09:30] Anika Patel: Could you show a flamechart expand?\\n[09:33] Ethan Zhou: Expanding now \u2014 see expanded kernel spans, GPU copy, enqueue, compute, postproc. You can hover to get the raw logs attached to a span.\\n[09:41] Jon Rivera: Raw logs \u2014 are they compressed?\\n[09:43] Ethan Zhou: Stored compressed in S3-like storage; UI decompresses on the fly.\\n[09:47] [09:47] Marcus Lee: On RBAC, can we limit who sees prompt text in the console?\\n[09:51] Lina Ortega: Yes. RBAC supports field-level permissions \u2014 you can revoke view of prompt_text for a role.\\n[09:56] Anika Patel: Nice.\\n[09:58] [09:58] Priya Malhotra: Quick pause for questions. Anything we haven't covered?\\n[10:02] Marcus Lee: What about cost tracking per-request so product can see token cost per feature?\\n[10:06] Ethan Zhou: We include token and cost estimates per request; Console has a cost explorer and per-route breakdowns.\\n[10:12] Anika Patel: Does that tie back to billing in the invoice?\\n[10:14] Priya Malhotra: Yes, you can map routes to billing codes and export usage for chargeback.\\n[10:19] [10:19] Jon Rivera: For troubleshooting, sometimes we want to replay a request against a different model variant. Do you support replay?\\n[10:24] Ethan Zhou: There's a Replay feature: you can re-run a historical request against another model or config in a sandbox without affecting production metrics. It logs the replay and provides diff of outputs.\\n[10:34] Marcus Lee: If the replay is run on hosted, are we exposing the original prompt again?\\n[10:38] Priya Malhotra: Replays respect the same data-retention and redaction policies \u2014 you can opt to replay with a scrubbed prompt.\\n[10:44] [10:44] Anika Patel: For the POC we want to capture 100% of errors and 1% of successes for the /summarize route, keep 90 days of traces, and push exports to our S3. Is that doable?\\n[10:53] Ethan Zhou: Yes \u2014 that's a typical POC setup. We'll size the storage and cost impact and provide recommendations.\\n[10:58] Priya Malhotra: Next steps recap: Priya will send tracing deck and short vid; Ethan will run a sample export and attach schema; Marcus to share compliance contact. We'll schedule POC scoping.\\n[11:10] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. A couple of quick real questions: Any gotchas with GDPR when exporting to US buckets?\\n[11:15] Lina Ortega: You can choose region for storage; for Hosted we store per-region by default. For cross-border you need lawful basis or anonymization. We'll share legal guidance.\\n[11:25] Anika Patel: One more \u2014 what if we hit a rare edge case where trace grouping mislabels root cause?\\n[11:30] Ethan Zhou: You can re-tag grouped clusters and feed that back; we use those labels to improve clustering heuristics.\\n[11:36] [11:36] Jon Rivera: Thanks, that helps.\\n[11:38] Priya Malhotra: Great. We'll follow up with the artifacts. Appreciate your time.\\n[11:42] Marcus Lee: Thanks everyone.\\n[11:44] [11:44] End of recording.",

    "Ethan to run a targeted request-log export/benchmark with BeaconHealth sample workload (by 2025-09-18)",
    "Marcus to confirm compliance contact and share SOC2 scope doc (by 2025-09-16)",
    "Schedule a 60-min POC scoping session with infra and security (target week of 2025-09-22)"
  ],
  "action_items": [
    "Ethan Zhou \u2014 export 2 hours of request logs + top error traces for BeaconHealth sample \u2014 2025-09-18",
    "Priya Malhotra \u2014 send security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, KMS notes) \u2014 2025-09-13",
    "Marcus Lee \u2014 share redacted sample request IDs and latency distribution \u2014 2025-09-15"
  ],
  "transcription_quality": "medium",
  "crm_deal_id": "CRM-57821",
  "summary": "AE/SE walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, request logs, and error analysis. Customer cares most about production debugging, PII handling in logs, and integration with their PagerDuty/SLOs. Agreed to run a small log export and benchmark, send security docs, and schedule POC scoping.",
  "topics": [
    "Console tracing UI",
    "Request logs export",
    "Error analysis and stack traces",
    "KV cache and request sampling",
    "Security (KMS, PII redaction)",
    "Canary and fallback flows"
  ],
  "transcript": "[00:00] Priya Malhotra: Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for carving out time. I'm Priya, AE on the account at Redwood, and with me is Ethan from our SE team and Lina from CS. Who do we have on from BeaconHealth?\\n[00:08] Marcus Lee: Marcus here, CTO. Anika is on as well and Jon from SRE. Hey.\\n[00:11] Anika Patel: Hi all.\\n[00:13] Priya Malhotra: Awesome. Objective today is a focused console walkthrough \u2014 specifically tracing, error analysis, and request logs \u2014 so you can see how we'd debug production flows. We'll leave Q&A and then outline next steps.\\n[00:22] Ethan Zhou: Quick note, I'll show live UI, and also a short demo of request-log export and how we attach top-k traces to failed requests.\\n[00:27] Jon Rivera: Great, we mostly care about root cause \u2014 why a particular generate call spiked latency \u2014 and how much PII could be in logs.\\n[00:32] Priya Malhotra: Perfect. I'll hand to Ethan.\\n[00:34] Ethan Zhou: Cool. Pulling up the Console \u2014 bear with me, sometimes the screen share resizes. Ok so this is the Requests view \u2014 you can filter by model, route, and timeframe.\\n[00:45] [00:45] Ethan Zhou: You see here request IDs on the left, status column, tokens consumed, and a small latency sparkline. We also have a column for \"trace score\" which indicates anomalous internal events.\\n[00:58] Anika Patel: That \"trace score\" \u2014 is that an actual statistical anomaly or heuristics?\\n[01:03] Ethan Zhou: It's heuristics + recent baseline. We run a rolling window of per-route medians and flag deviations beyond configurable thresholds. There is an API to pull raw metrics if you want to plug into your own alerting.\\n[01:15] Marcus Lee: How granular are the traces? We want per-shard, GPU-level timing if possible.\\n[01:20] Ethan Zhou: Good question. Traces are hierarchical. We capture request->model-inference->kernel stages. For Dedicated and Private installs we can surface device-level timings \u2014 e.g., GPU copy, kernel invocation \u2014 but in Hosted we give aggregated node-level times and key stage durations. Sometimes the product name gets scrambled in the transcript \u2014 uh, sorry \u2014 I mean we surface the important spans.\\n[01:39] Jon Rivera: And KV cache hits? Can I see cache hit ratio per request?\\n[01:42] Ethan Zhou: Yes, we annotate spans with KV cache metadata \u2014 hit, miss, partial hit \u2014 and you can filter by that. That shows up in the span details pane.\\n[01:48] [01:48] Ethan Zhou: Example: here is a request that had a 95% token increase and we can see a spike in model-generation span because KV cache was a miss.\\n[01:55] Anika Patel: Hmm, can we mask prompt text? We can't have raw PHI in the console.\\n[02:00] Priya Malhotra: Important point \u2014 we offer PII redaction at ingest and masking in the UI. For Hosted we can redact at collection time per-route; for Private you can enforce no prompt text collection or use customer-side redaction before sending.\\n[02:11] Marcus Lee: What's the retention on request logs by default?\\n[02:14] Lina Ortega: Default retention is 30 days for hosted by tier, but we have enterprise options to increase retention and export to your S3 or your SIEM.\\n[02:22] Marcus Lee: Export \u2014 what's the format?\\n[02:24] Ethan Zhou: Exports are JSONL with per-request metadata + span arrays. We can also stream to your Kinesis or put to S3 with encryption via your KMS.\\n[02:33] Jon Rivera: If we want to run an offline analysis, can we request a subset? Like all 5xxs for a given route in a timeframe?\\n[02:39] Ethan Zhou: Yep. Filters support status codes, route, model, latency thresholds, KV cache tags, any metadata tag. You can export filtered results or run an ad-hoc query in Console and then export.\\n[02:47] [02:47] Marcus Lee: Walk me through a failure example \u2014 we've had a case where latency randomly jumps from 80ms to 3s.\\n[02:53] Ethan Zhou: Sure \u2014 here's an example trace. At 00:00 request enters. The pre-proc span shows 20ms, model-infer shows 2.9s. Looking into the kernel-level annotations we see a GPU memory copy stall and then a fallback to CPU quantized path \u2014 so a model cold-start or memory pressure event. In Dedicated this would be surfaced as device OOM hints.\\n[03:14] Anika Patel: How do you detect fallback to different model variants?\\n[03:18] Ethan Zhou: We attach a \"served-with\" tag to request metadata \u2014 e.g., redwood/llama-2-q8_64 \u2014 and if a fallback occurs we show the fallback chain and reason.\\n[03:26] Marcus Lee: You mentioned canary and fallback policies earlier \u2014 can the console show rollout state?\\n[03:30] Priya Malhotra: Yes, Rollouts view shows percentage traffic, models in the pool, and automatic fallback logs. For example, if latency breaches SLO on a canary, the system can auto-failover to the stable variant and we log that as an event with request IDs.\\n[03:43] Jon Rivera: Ok. On SSO and auditing \u2014 we need per-request audit logs forwarding to Splunk.\\n[03:48] Lina Ortega: We support audit log forwarding, SAML-based SSO, RBAC and granular token-level audit. The audit logs are separate from request logs and are forwarded in real-time.\\n[03:58] Anika Patel: Do audit logs include the prompt?\\n[04:00] Priya Malhotra: By default audit logs include metadata about actions (who pulled export, who changed rollout) but not prompt content unless you enable deeper logging. For compliance we can turn off prompt capture.\\n[04:10] [04:10] Marcus Lee: How about encryption at rest and in transit? We use customer-managed KMS for keys in private deployments.\\n[04:16] Ethan Zhou: In Hosted we manage keys but we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private. All transfers use TLS and S3 exports can be encrypted with your KMS prefix.\\n[04:25] Jon Rivera: Great. Let's talk about sampling \u2014 we can't keep full logs for 100% of traffic.\\n[04:29] Ethan Zhou: Absolutely. We have adaptive sampling policies: deterministic sampling (e.g., 1% of requests), error-triggered sampling (capture all 5xx and 4xx above X ms), and stratified sampling by route. You can configure per-route sampling and we persist the sampling decision in headers for correlation.\\n[04:44] Anika Patel: Does adaptive sampling break debugging of rare errors?\\n[04:47] Ethan Zhou: We recommend error-triggered capture so you always capture a representative set of failures. You can temporarily override sampling for a route during an incident.\\n[04:55] [04:55] Marcus Lee: On the traces, sometimes we have batch requests that fan out \u2014 can I see correlation across sub-requests?\\n[05:00] Ethan Zhou: Yes, we maintain trace parent-child IDs and present them in a flamechart. For batched fan-outs you can collapse or expand spans and view combined latency vs per-subreq.\\n[05:09] Priya Malhotra: Quick note: some transcriptions may show product names slightly off, for instance \"Rudwood\" instead of Redwood \u2014 ignore that, sorry.\\n[05:17] Anika Patel: (laughs) got it.\\n[05:19] [05:19] Jon Rivera: Can we create alerts from the Console based on trace-level conditions?\\n[05:22] Ethan Zhou: Yes, alerting rules can be set on aggregated metrics or on trace conditions like repeated 'GPU copy stall' events, error rate per route, or tail latency percentiles. Alerts can notify Slack, PagerDuty, or webhooks.\\n[05:33] Marcus Lee: Do you keep a mapping between request IDs and downstream tool logs? We use Heka/Fluentd and want to correlate.\\n[05:39] Ethan Zhou: We support correlation IDs \u2014 you can inject your trace-id into request metadata and our export preserves it. We also can push logs to your syslog and provide a mapping table.\\n[05:47] Anika Patel: Let's talk about a real integration scenario: we want an on-call flow where SRE sees the trace, then clicks a CTA to open a PagerDuty incident with pre-populated context.\\n[05:56] Ethan Zhou: That's supported. There's an \"Open Incident\" action that creates a PagerDuty incident with link to the trace and attaches the top 5 traces as JSON. You can also set runbooks or internal notes.\\n[06:05] [06:05] Marcus Lee: Okay would love to see a quick example of exporting error traces to S3.\\n[06:09] Ethan Zhou: I'll trigger a filter for status:5xx, last 2 hours, route: /summarize. Running export... and sending to the configured S3 bucket \u2014 job queued. In this demo I've used a sandbox bucket; for production we'd wire to your account.\\n[06:25] Anika Patel: You said job queued \u2014 how long does it take?\\n[06:28] Ethan Zhou: Depends on volume; for a couple of thousand records typically under a minute. For a large export we chunk and compress.\\n[06:35] Jon Rivera: Any throttling concerns?\\n[06:37] Ethan Zhou: Exports are rate-limited per account, but you can request higher quotas for POC. Also we support incremental exports.\\n[06:44] [06:44] Anika Patel: Can we get the exported payload schema before we wire the consumer?\\n[06:48] Priya Malhotra: Yes \u2014 Ethan will drop a schema doc along with the sample export and a small script to map fields into your ELK.\\n[06:55] Ethan Zhou: On error analysis, Console surfaces top-N stack traces and groups by root cause using a similarity heuristic. It's not perfect \u2014 sometimes semantically different errors are grouped \u2014 but we provide filters to re-cluster.\\n[07:07] Marcus Lee: Similarity heuristic \u2014 is that ML based?\\n[07:10] Ethan Zhou: It's a hybrid: token-based fingerprinting plus some ML features for fuzzy matching. You can tune sensitivity.\\n[07:17] [07:17] Anika Patel: Let's talk about the Optimize recommendations \u2014 this is slightly adjacent but useful.\\n[07:21] Priya Malhotra: Redwood Optimize will recommend batching and quantization profiles by route. The Console surfaces potential token savings and projected cost delta if you switch to q4_0 or to a smaller model variant.\\n[07:33] Marcus Lee: How accurate are those cost projections?\\n[07:35] Ethan Zhou: They use historical per-token distributions, request sizes, and our kernel throughput models. Typically within 5-10% of observed cost after rollout, though will vary with traffic changes.\\n[07:45] Jon Rivera: For an internal POC we'll likely try Dedicated or Private \u2014 will tracing differ?\\n[07:50] Ethan Zhou: In Dedicated and Private you get more granular device-level traces and more control over retention and encryption. The console UI is the same; only the backend telemetry granularity changes.\\n[08:01] Anika Patel: Are there any limitations when using Private in an air-gapped environment?\\n[08:05] Priya Malhotra: In air-gapped on-prem deployments we ship a collector that runs internally and writes to your internal object store. You still get the Console control plane if it's VPC-connected; fully air-gapped installs have a local Console bundle. We can share topology guides.\\n[08:18] [08:18] Marcus Lee: Security: does Eks or GKE integration affect trace collection? We run on GKE.\\n[08:22] Ethan Zhou: We provide a sidecar collector or daemonset that extracts telemetry before it leaves your cluster. For GKE/EKS we have Kubernetes integration docs.\\n[08:30] Anika Patel: If we want to disable prompt capture globally, but enable it for a single route temporarily, is that straightforward?\\n[08:35] Ethan Zhou: Yes \u2014 per-route telemetry flags allow you to override default collection settings. You can also set a time-based override.\\n[08:42] [08:42] Jon Rivera: Let's talk cost implications of verbose tracing \u2014 how much does it add?\\n[08:46] Ethan Zhou: Depends on sampling and retention. Full payload capture at high volume can add storage and egress costs; Optimize will estimate this and suggest sampling or export-only-on-errors patterns.\\n[08:56] Marcus Lee: Any customers using 100% of traces in production?\\n[08:59] Ethan Zhou: Very few. Most use targeted capture plus full capture for important routes.\\n[09:04] [09:04] Anika Patel: Do you anonymize tokens when redacting? Like preserve token counts but mask content?\\n[09:09] Priya Malhotra: We can mask or hash token content while preserving lengths and token boundaries for analysis. Good for privacy-preserving debugging.\\n[09:18] Marcus Lee: About the UI, is there an API to fetch the same traces programmatically? We want to integrate into our incident tooling.\\n[09:23] Ethan Zhou: Absolutely. There's a Request Logs API; you can paginate, supply filters, and get signed URLs for exports.\\n[09:30] [09:30] Anika Patel: Could you show a flamechart expand?\\n[09:33] Ethan Zhou: Expanding now \u2014 see expanded kernel spans, GPU copy, enqueue, compute, postproc. You can hover to get the raw logs attached to a span.\\n[09:41] Jon Rivera: Raw logs \u2014 are they compressed?\\n[09:43] Ethan Zhou: Stored compressed in S3-like storage; UI decompresses on the fly.\\n[09:47] [09:47] Marcus Lee: On RBAC, can we limit who sees prompt text in the console?\\n[09:51] Lina Ortega: Yes. RBAC supports field-level permissions \u2014 you can revoke view of prompt_text for a role.\\n[09:56] Anika Patel: Nice.\\n[09:58] [09:58] Priya Malhotra: Quick pause for questions. Anything we haven't covered?\\n[10:02] Marcus Lee: What about cost tracking per-request so product can see token cost per feature?\\n[10:06] Ethan Zhou: We include token and cost estimates per request; Console has a cost explorer and per-route breakdowns.\\n[10:12] Anika Patel: Does that tie back to billing in the invoice?\\n[10:14] Priya Malhotra: Yes, you can map routes to billing codes and export usage for chargeback.\\n[10:19] [10:19] Jon Rivera: For troubleshooting, sometimes we want to replay a request against a different model variant. Do you support replay?\\n[10:24] Ethan Zhou: There's a Replay feature: you can re-run a historical request against another model or config in a sandbox without affecting production metrics. It logs the replay and provides diff of outputs.\\n[10:34] Marcus Lee: If the replay is run on hosted, are we exposing the original prompt again?\\n[10:38] Priya Malhotra: Replays respect the same data-retention and redaction policies \u2014 you can opt to replay with a scrubbed prompt.\\n[10:44] [10:44] Anika Patel: For the POC we want to capture 100% of errors and 1% of successes for the /summarize route, keep 90 days of traces, and push exports to our S3. Is that doable?\\n[10:53] Ethan Zhou: Yes \u2014 that's a typical POC setup. We'll size the storage and cost impact and provide recommendations.\\n[10:58] Priya Malhotra: Next steps recap: Priya will send tracing deck and short vid; Ethan will run a sample export and attach schema; Marcus to share compliance contact. We'll schedule POC scoping.\\n[11:10] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. A couple of quick real questions: Any gotchas with GDPR when exporting to US buckets?\\n[11:15] Lina Ortega: You can choose region for storage; for Hosted we store per-region by default. For cross-border you need lawful basis or anonymization. We'll share legal guidance.\\n[11:25] Anika Patel: One more \u2014 what if we hit a rare edge case where trace grouping mislabels root cause?\\n[11:30] Ethan Zhou: You can re-tag grouped clusters and feed that back; we use those labels to improve clustering heuristics.\\n[11:36] [11:36] Jon Rivera: Thanks, that helps.\\n[11:38] Priya Malhotra: Great.     "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Consumption Sampling & Preview Playbook\",\n  \"space\": \"product-docs\",\n  \"author\": \"Priya Menon\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"product\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-09-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-10-12\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Eliot Carter\",\n    \"Marta Ruiz\",\n    \"Jun Park\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"consumption\",\n    \"preview\",\n    \"pricing\",\n    \"sampling\",\n    \"onboarding\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/product-docs/product-overview/consumption-playground-developer-onboarding-overview-2026-03-22.json\",\n    \"/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/elastic-session-crediting-and-migration-playbook-2029-04-03.json\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Summary\\n\\nThis playbook describes the design, product rules, and rollout plan for Redwood's Consumption Sampling & Preview feature: a low-friction mechanism to (1) sample a small percentage of new/developer traffic, (2) deliver a preview-quality response surface to end users or integrators, and (3) apply special preview billing or crediting semantics. The goal is to improve trial conversion, reduce onboarding cost for exploratory users, and capture production-like telemetry for fidelity/quality evaluation without full-priced consumption.\\n\\nIntended audience\\n- Product managers and PMMs running developer growth experiments\\n- SDK and Console UX teams implementing preview flows\\n- Billing and finance for pricing/credit rules\\n- Serving/runtime and infra engineers responsible for sampling proxies and telemetry\\n- Customer success for onboarding playbooks\\n\\nScope and non-goals\\n- In-scope: HTTP/SDK-level sampling controls, preview-quality response tagging, per-tenant preview quotas, preview billing hooks, telemetry and SLOs for preview flows, UI affordances in Console for enabling previews.\\n- Out-of-scope: full-fidelity model variant rollouts, on-prem private-preview billing (handled separately by Private deployments billing), and agent-based interactive sampling (future work).\\n\\nProduct rules and definitions\\n- Preview request: ANY request flagged via header X-Redwood-Preview: true or initiated from Console \\\"Enable Preview\\\" is treated as a preview request.\\n- Sampling window: default 7 days per tenant for new signups; configurable.\\n- Preview quota: default 1000 preview tokens / tenant / 7-day window. Can be increased by entitlement.\\n- Billing model: preview tokens are billed at a discounted rate or consumed from promotional credits. Ledger events must include preview=true.\\n\\nHigh-level flow\\n1. New tenant signs up or developer toggles Preview in the Console.\\n2. Platform routes preview-flagged requests to the preview path in the routing layer.\\n3. Serving runtime applies lightweight fidelity policy (see Fidelity policy matrix).\\n4. Telemetry is emitted with preview tags; billing pipeline associates usage with preview ledger and discount rules.\\n\\nFidelity policy matrix (default)\\n| Use case | Fidelity level | Model variant | Latency SLO | Token cap per response | Notes |\\n|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|\\n| Quick API explore | low | quantized-compatible | p95 < 300ms | 512 | Fast, cost-efficient preview |\\n| Code / structured output preview | medium | base-compat | p95 < 600ms | 2048 | Prefer stable tokenization |\\n| Chat-style end-to-end preview | medium-high | base-with-kv | p95 < 800ms | 4096 | Keep streaming enabled if requested |\\n\\nConfiguration knobs (Console + API)\\n- sample_rate: 0.0 - 1.0 (per-tenant or global). Default new-tenant sample_rate = 0.25 for first 48 hours, then 0.05 for days 3-7.\\n- preview_quota: integer tokens (default 1000).\\n- preview_billing_mode: [credit_consumption, discounted_billable, free].\\n- preview_variant_whitelist: list of model-variant ids allowed for previews.\\n\\nAPI examples\\n- Enable preview via header (SDK):\\n  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \\\\\\\\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \\\\\\\\n    -H 'X-Redwood-Preview: true' \\\\\\\\n    -d '{\\\"model\\\":\\\"rwd-base-1\\\",\\\"input\\\":\\\"Summarize the report\\\"}'\\n\\n- Console toggle creates tenant-level flag and sets sample_rate and preview_quota.\\n\\nBilling and ledger requirements\\n- Every preview request must emit a billable_event with preview:true. The billing pipeline must:\\n  1) Deduct from preview credits if preview_billing_mode == credit_consumption.\\n  2) If credits exhausted and mode == discounted_billable, apply 50% of standard token rate.\\n  3) If mode == free, generate non-billable ledger events for marketing analysis (still subject to quota).\\n\\nTelemetry and SLOs\\n- Telemetry fields (required): preview (bool), preview_quota_remaining (int), preview_mode (string), sample_rate (float).\\n- SLOs for preview traffic (platform-level): p95 latency <= baseline_p95 * 1.5; error rate < 1% absolute above baseline errors.\\n- Monitoring dashboards (recommended): preview-traffic-ratio, preview-quota-burn-rate, preview-conversion-lift, preview-telemetry-anomalies.\\n\\n rollout plan and gating\\n1. Canary (week 0) \\u2014 Internal tenants + 5 developer orgs. sample_rate = 1.0, preview_quota = 5000, preview_billing_mode = free. Objective: validate telemetry, routing and billing tags.\\n2. Beta (week 2) \\u2014 Open to self-serve signups with sample_rate defaults. Objective: UX polish and conversion measurement.\\n3. Gradual ramp (week 6-12) \\u2014 Adjust sample_rate per cohort using A/B testing; enable discounted_billable for high-usage tiers.\\n4. GA (quarterly milestone) \\u2014 Full console and SDK docs, productized pricing bundles for preview credits.\\n\\nRollout checklists\\n- Serving/runtime: implement preview routing path, ensure KV cache isolation for preview flows, and add preview tag to traces.\\n- Billing: ensure ledger event schema includes preview fields and promo-credit reconciliation implemented.\\n- Console/UX: toggle + quota view, endpoint-level greyed badge for previewed responses.\\n- Growth/PMM: default messaging, email drip for preview expiry, and funnel tracking enabled.\\n\\nGuardrails and risk mitigation\\n- Abuse detection: set default per-IP and per-key rate limits for preview flows. Flag tenants exceeding 3x expected preview burn-rate for manual review.\\n- Data residency: preview requests are subject to same residency rules; do not route preview traffic out-of-region for isolated tenants.\\n- Privacy: annotate preview responses with metadata to exclude them from public benchmark data unless tenant opt-in is given.\\n\\nOperational playbooks (incident examples)\\n- If preview_quota burn unexpectedly spikes:\\n  1) Auto-throttle sample_rate by 50% for affected tenant(s).\\n  2) Notify CS and owning PM via Slack channel #preview-ops.\\n  3) Create a ticket and assign to runtime-oncall.\\n- If preview billing mis-attributed:\\n  1) Pause ledger ingestion for preview events.\\n  2) Re-run the reconciliation job with corrected mapping within 6 hours.\\n\\nMeasurement and success metrics (examples)\\n- Conversion lift: % of preview users who convert to paying within 14 days (target +8% for cohort A).\\n- Cost per converted user: preview credit spend / conversions (target < $120).\\n- Telemetry quality: % of preview sessions with complete trace and tokens captured (target > 98%).\\n\\nOpen questions and roadmap items\\n- Multi-variant previewing: should previews be allowed to hit newer 'canary' model variants for evaluation without impacting billing? (risk: customer confusion).\\n- Cross-tenant preview telemetry aggregation: how to provide aggregated benchmarking while preserving tenant anonymity.\\n- On-prem preview semantics: define preview_billing_mode for Private deployments (legal review required).\\n\\nOwnership and contacts\\n- Product owner: Priya Menon (product)\\n- Runtime owner: Eliot Carter (eng-serving-runtime)\\n- Billing owner: Marta Ruiz (finance-legal)\\n- CS & Onboarding: Jun Park (customer-success)\\n\\nRelated artifacts and links\\n- Implementation RFC: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/preview-routing-rfc-2026-09-01 (internal)\\n- Billing schema spec: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/preview-ledger-schema-2026-08-20 (internal)\\n- UX mocks: /drive/redwood/preview-toggle-mocks-2026-09-10 (design drive)\\n\\nAppendix: example preview configuration (YAML)\\npreview_config:\\n  enabled: true\\n  sample_rate: 0.25\\n  quota_tokens: 1000\\n  billing_mode: credit_consumption\\n  whitelist_variants:\\n    - rwd-base-1\\n    - rwd-quant-lite-1\\n\\nAppendix: minimal telemetry event (JSON)\\n{\\n  \\\"event\\\": \\\"generation.request\\\",\\n  \\\"tenant_id\\\": \\\"t-123\\\",\\n  \\\"preview\\\": true,\\n  \\\"tokens\\\": 142,\\n  \\\"preview_quota_remaining\\\": 858\\n}\\n\\nRevision history\\n- 2026-09-15: Draft created by Priya Menon.\\n- 2026-09-22: Added telemetry and billing requirements (reviewers: Eliot Carter, Marta Ruiz).\\n- 2026-10-12: Finalized rollout plan and guardrails; published.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_78e8f35d4d9945529de4157b5241bec9\"\n}",

document.title: Consumption Sampling & Preview Playbook
document.content:
{
  "title": "Consumption Sampling & Preview Playbook",
  "space": "product-docs",
  "author": "Priya Menon",
  "owner_team": "product",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-09-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-10-12",
  "reviewers": [
    "Eliot Carter",
    "Marta Ruiz",
    "Jun Park"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "consumption",
    "preview",
    "pricing",
    "sampling",
    "onboarding"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/product-docs/product-overview/consumption-playground-developer-onboarding-overview-2026-03-22.json",
    "/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/elastic-session-crediting-and-migration-playbook-2029-04-03.json"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Summary

This playbook describes the design, product rules, and rollout plan for Redwood's Consumption Sampling & Preview feature: a low-friction mechanism to (1) sample a small percentage of new/developer traffic, (2) deliver a preview-quality response surface to end users or integrators, and (3) apply special preview billing or crediting semantics. The goal is to improve trial conversion, reduce onboarding cost for exploratory users, and capture production-like telemetry for fidelity/quality evaluation without full-priced consumption.

Intended audience
- Product managers and PMMs running developer growth experiments
- SDK and Console UX teams implementing preview flows
- Billing and finance for pricing/credit rules
- Serving/runtime and infra engineers responsible for sampling proxies and telemetry
- Customer success for onboarding playbooks

Scope and non-goals
- In-scope: HTTP/SDK-level sampling controls, preview-quality response tagging, per-tenant preview quotas, preview billing hooks, telemetry and SLOs for preview flows, UI affordances in Console for enabling previews.
- Out-of-scope: full-fidelity model variant rollouts, on-prem private-preview billing (handled separately by Private deployments billing), and agent-based interactive sampling (future work).

Product rules and definitions
- Preview request: ANY request flagged via header X-Redwood-Preview: true or initiated from Console "Enable Preview" is treated as a preview request.
- Sampling window: default 7 days per tenant for new signups; configurable.
- Preview quota: default 1000 preview tokens / tenant / 7-day window. Can be increased by entitlement.
- Billing model: preview tokens are billed at a discounted rate or consumed from promotional credits. Ledger events must include preview=true.

High-level flow
1. New tenant signs up or developer toggles Preview in the Console.
2. Platform routes preview-flagged requests to the preview path in the routing layer.
3. Serving runtime applies lightweight fidelity policy (see Fidelity policy matrix).
4. Telemetry is emitted with preview tags; billing pipeline associates usage with preview ledger and discount rules.

Fidelity policy matrix (default)
| Use case | Fidelity level | Model variant | Latency SLO | Token cap per response | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| Quick API explore | low | quantized-compatible | p95 < 300ms | 512 | Fast, cost-efficient preview |
| Code / structured output preview | medium | base-compat | p95 < 600ms | 2048 | Prefer stable tokenization |
| Chat-style end-to-end preview | medium-high | base-with-kv | p95 < 800ms | 4096 | Keep streaming enabled if requested |

Configuration knobs (Console + API)
- sample_rate: 0.0 - 1.0 (per-tenant or global). Default new-tenant sample_rate = 0.25 for first 48 hours, then 0.05 for days 3-7.
- preview_quota: integer tokens (default 1000).
- preview_billing_mode: [credit_consumption, discounted_billable, free].
- preview_variant_whitelist: list of model-variant ids allowed for previews.

API examples
- Enable preview via header (SDK):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \\n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \\n    -H 'X-Redwood-Preview: true' \\n    -d '{"model":"rwd-base-1","input":"Summarize the report"}'

- Console toggle creates tenant-level flag and sets sample_rate and preview_quota.

Billing and ledger requirements
- Every preview request must emit a billable_event with preview:true. The billing pipeline must:
  1) Deduct from preview credits if preview_billing_mode == credit_consumption.
  2) If credits exhausted and mode == discounted_billable, apply 50% of standard token rate.
  3) If mode == free, generate non-billable ledger events for marketing analysis (still subject to quota).

Telemetry and SLOs
- Telemetry fields (required): preview (bool), preview_quota_remaining (int), preview_mode (string), sample_rate (float).
- SLOs for preview traffic (platform-level): p95 latency <= baseline_p95 * 1.5; error rate < 1% absolute above baseline errors.
- Monitoring dashboards (recommended): preview-traffic-ratio, preview-quota-burn-rate, preview-conversion-lift, preview-telemetry-anomalies.

 rollout plan and gating
1. Canary (week 0) — Internal tenants + 5 developer orgs. sample_rate = 1.0, preview_quota = 5000, preview_billing_mode = free. Objective: validate telemetry, routing and billing tags.
2. Beta (week 2) — Open to self-serve signups with sample_rate defaults. Objective: UX polish and conversion measurement.
3. Gradual ramp (week 6-12) — Adjust sample_rate per cohort using A/B testing; enable discounted_billable for high-usage tiers.
4. GA (quarterly milestone) — Full console and SDK docs, productized pricing bundles for preview credits.

Rollout checklists
- Serving/runtime: implement preview routing path, ensure KV cache isolation for preview flows, and add preview tag to traces.
- Billing: ensure ledger event schema includes preview fields and promo-credit reconciliation implemented.
- Console/UX: toggle + quota view, endpoint-level greyed badge for previewed responses.
- Growth/PMM: default messaging, email drip for preview expiry, and funnel tracking enabled.

Guardrails and risk mitigation
- Abuse detection: set default per-IP and per-key rate limits for preview flows. Flag tenants exceeding 3x expected preview burn-rate for manual review.
- Data residency: preview requests are subject to same residency rules; do not route preview traffic out-of-region for isolated tenants.
- Privacy: annotate preview responses with metadata to exclude them from public benchmark data unless tenant opt-in is given.

Operational playbooks (incident examples)
- If preview_quota burn unexpectedly spikes:
  1) Auto-throttle sample_rate by 50% for affected tenant(s).
  2) Notify CS and owning PM via Slack channel #preview-ops.
  3) Create a ticket and assign to runtime-oncall.
- If preview billing mis-attributed:
  1) Pause ledger ingestion for preview events.
  2) Re-run the reconciliation job with corrected mapping within 6 hours.

Measurement and success metrics (examples)
- Conversion lift: % of preview users who convert to paying within 14 days (target +8% for cohort A).
- Cost per converted user: preview credit spend / conversions (target < $120).
- Telemetry quality: % of preview sessions with complete trace and tokens captured (target > 98%).

Open questions and roadmap items
- Multi-variant previewing: should previews be allowed to hit newer 'canary' model variants for evaluation without impacting billing? (risk: customer confusion).
- Cross-tenant preview telemetry aggregation: how to provide aggregated benchmarking while preserving tenant anonymity.
- On-prem preview semantics: define preview_billing_mode for Private deployments (legal review required).

Ownership and contacts
- Product owner: Priya Menon (product)
- Runtime owner: Eliot Carter (eng-serving-runtime)
- Billing owner: Marta Ruiz (finance-legal)
- CS & Onboarding: Jun Park (customer-success)

Related artifacts and links
- Implementation RFC: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/preview-routing-rfc-2026-09-01 (internal)
- Billing schema spec: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/preview-ledger-schema-2026-08-20 (internal)
- UX mocks: /drive/redwood/preview-toggle-mocks-2026-09-10 (design drive)

Appendix: example preview configuration (YAML)
preview_config:
  enabled: true
  sample_rate: 0.25
  quota_tokens: 1000
  billing_mode: credit_consumption
  whitelist_variants:
    - rwd-base-1
    - rwd-quant-lite-1

Appendix: minimal telemetry event (JSON)
{
  "event": "generation.request",
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "preview": true,
  "tokens": 142,
  "preview_quota_remaining": 858
}

Revision history
- 2026-09-15: Draft created by Priya Menon.
- 2026-09-22: Added telemetry and billing requirements (reviewers: Eliot Carter, Marta Ruiz).
- 2026-10-12: Finalized rollout plan and guardrails; published.",

    "body"
  ],

    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"20487\",\n  \"title\": \"unified-api-observability-add-requestid-trace-propagation-and-per-endpoint-metrics-tags\",\n  \"author\": \"Lina Chen\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-02-23\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2026-02-23\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/api-observability-unified-ids\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Evan Brooks\",\n    \"Miguel Alvarez\",\n    \"Priya Nair\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"api\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"runtime\",\n    \"perf\",\n    \"docs\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-1248\",\n    \"ENG-1302\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"12\",\n  \"additions\": \"780\",\n  \"deletions\": \"210\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"Added request id + trace propagation across API surface, structured logs with request/trace fields, per-endpoint metrics tags, and OpenAI-compatibility header mapping. No user-visible breaking changes; opt-in header behavior documented.\",\n  \"description\": \"Motivation: Production incidents and customer feedback showed gaps in observability across the public API surface: missing/unstable request ids for streaming responses, inconsistent trace propagation through the OpenAI compatibility layer, and insufficient per-endpoint metric tags for cost/latency attribution. This PR adds a unified request ID and trace propagation model, structured JSON logging augmentation, and per-endpoint metrics tags so latency/cost dashboards and alerting can attribute behavior correctly.\\\\n\\\\nWhat this change does (summary): - Assigns a stable request_id at the API ingress for every request (hosted/dedicated/private). The request_id is included as: X-Request-Id response header, a top-level field in structured JSON logs (request_id), and injected into streaming chunk envelopes so that partial responses can be correlated to a single request. - Propagates tracing headers (traceparent and b3 where present) to internal services and exporters; integrates with our OpenTelemetry pipeline. We canonicalize trace ids to trace_id in structured logs. - Enhances the OpenAI compatibility layer: preserve incoming OpenAI-style request ids (if present) and map them onto internal request_id while returning OpenAI-compatible response ids; ensure the x-request-id header is forwarded and mirrored to openai response 'id'. - Adds per-endpoint and per-model metric tags (route, operation, model.family) emitted to metrics backend so dashboards can slice latency and token cost by API route (completion/chat/embeddings), model family, and plan tier. - Structured log fields: request_id, trace_id, route, http_method, user_id (when present), model, tokens_in, tokens_out, response_status, tool_call_id (for function/tool calls). - Streaming stability changes: ensure server assigns request_id before handshake completes with client; streaming chunks now include metadata envelopes with request_id and sequence numbers. This reduces misattribution for aborted/partial streams. - Function/tool calling observability: each tool call receives a tool_call_id and is correlated to the parent request trace; logs include tool_call_id/tool_name and duration. - Tests and CI: unit tests for header mapping, integration tests for streaming chunk envelopes, and a smoke test to validate metrics tags are emitted.\\\\n\\\\nDesign notes: - We intentionally keep the internal canonical ID as rr_request_id but expose it as X-Request-Id for HTTP compatibility and map it to OpenAI 'id' when using the compatibility endpoint. This avoids breaking customers who rely on existing OpenAI response id semantics while giving internal services a consistent key. - Trace propagation supports both W3C traceparent and B3. When both are present we prefer W3C and log both in debug mode. Traces are exported via our existing Otel collector config; no schema changes to the tracing backend. - Metrics tag cardinality is constrained: model.family is used rather than full model version in high-cardinality metrics. Route is normalized (chat.completions -> chat, completions -> completion, embeddings -> embedding). - Streaming envelope format: each chunk begins with a lightweight JSON prefix: {\\\"request_id\\\":\\\"...\\\",\\\"seq\\\":42,\\\"trace_id\\\":\\\"...\\\"} followed by payload. The prefix is base64-safe and parsed by our SDKs; fallback behavior: legacy clients ignoring the prefix still receive the payload uninterrupted (we validated parsing safety).\\\\n\\\\nFiles changed (high level): - api/gateway/handler.go: assign request_id early, header mapping, trace extraction. - api/gateway/streaming.go: chunk envelope implementation and handshake update. - compat/openai/translator.go: map x-request-id <-> openai id and ensure streaming envelope compatibility. - runtime/observability/logging.go: structured logger helpers and keys. - runtime/observability/metrics.go: metric tag extraction and emission code, tag normalization helpers. - runtime/tooling/tool-calls.go: tool_call_id generation and correlation instrumentation. - integration_tests/test_observability_streaming.py: end-to-end streaming + header assertions. - unit_tests/test_openai_compat_header_mapping.go: mapping edge cases. - docs/api/observability.md: new docs section explaining headers, logs, and metric tags.\\\\n\\\\nCommits (summary): - 0a3d8f2: initial gateway instrumentation and request id generation - 3b9f1c7: implement streaming chunk envelopes and SDK-friendly prefix - b1e4c6a: add OpenAI compatibility header mapping and translator tests - 6f7d2a1: structured logger helpers and trace canonicalization - f2c11b9: metrics tags emission and normalization + unit tests - 9d2b4e0: tool calling instrumentation and tool_call_id propagation - a7e8f33: docs and changelog entry; added rollout plan\\\\n\\\\nTesting and CI notes: - Initial CI run had an intermittent failure in streaming integration (integration_tests/test_observability_streaming.py) due to race on request_id injection; fixed by ensuring request_id is assigned before stream handshake completes and adding a short synchronization point in the test harness. - All unit tests + integration tests passing after fixes; end-to-end smoke run on staging validated traces appear in OTEL backend with correct trace_id and request_id tags, and metrics dashboard received route/model tags. CI status: pass.\\\\n\\\\nReview conversation (high level): - Miguel Alvarez: \\\"Can we avoid increasing tag cardinality for metrics? We should prefer model.family not full model names.\\\" Author reply: \\\"Agree \\u2014 changed emission to use model.family for high volume metrics; full model appears only in debug traces.\\\" - Priya Nair: \\\"Will OpenAI compat clients see any header changes?\\\" Author reply: \\\"No breaking change. We mirror internal rr_request_id to openai 'id' and return X-Request-Id as before. We document a new X-Redwood-Request-Id alias for debug.\\\" - Evan Brooks: \\\"Streaming envelope looks good. Make sure SDKs handle prefix safely.\\\" Author reply: \\\"Added parsing helpers in SDK interface and verified TS+Python SDK unit tests in their repos in follow-up PRs.\\\" - QA (Marcos): \\\"Observed a case where aborted streams left dangling metrics. Can you increment a 'stream.aborted' metric?\\\" Author reply: \\\"Added stream.aborted counter emitted when connection closed before final chunk; included in metrics change set.\\\"\\\\n\\\\nBackward compatibility and rollout: - Backwards compatible by default. Legacy clients that ignore the chunk envelope still receive payload; envelopes are designed to be safely ignored if not parsed. - Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag. Step 1: deploy to staging and run smoke tests (done). Step 2: deploy to canary subset of Hosted API (5% traffic) for 24 hours and monitor error/latency/trace correspondence dashboards. Step 3: full rollout with a 1h pause and rollback criteria defined in docs. We used canary run results to validate no increase in tail latency.\\\\n\\\\nOperational impact and alerts: - New dashboards added: API Request ID heatmap, Route x Model latency with request_id tagging, Streaming chunk success rate. - Alerts: increase in stream.aborted > 0.5% over baseline, mismatch count where request_id missing in logs > 0.1% of requests, and drop in trace sampling/ingestion.\\\\n\\\\nFollow-ups and TODOs: - SDK PRs to consume streaming prefix and surface request_id in client logs (TS+Python open follow-up PRs). - Instrument cost attribution pipeline to use model.family metric tags for billing experiments. - Add optional opt-out header X-Redwood-No-Request-Id for customers with specific privacy constraints (follow-up RFC).\\\\n\\\\nSummary: This PR improves end-to-end observability of Redwood's API surface by unifying request IDs, ensuring trace propagation throughout the stack, adding structured logs and per-endpoint metric tags, and keeping compatibility with OpenAI-style clients. The change was reviewed, tested, and merged (squash merge) to main on 2026-02-23.\",\n  \"commits_summary\": [\n    \"initial gateway instrumentation and request id generation\",\n    \"implement streaming chunk envelopes and SDK-friendly prefix\",\n    \"add OpenAI compatibility header mapping and translator tests\",\n    \"structured logger helpers and trace canonicalization\",\n    \"metrics tags emission and normalization + unit tests\",\n    \"tool calling instrumentation and tool_call_id propagation\",\n    \"docs and changelog entry; added rollout plan\"\n  ],\n  \"files_changed_list\": [\n    \"api/gateway/handler.go\",\n    \"api/gateway/streaming.go\",\n    \"compat/openai/translator.go\",\n    \"runtime/observability/logging.go\",\n    \"runtime/observability/metrics.go\",\n    \"runtime/tooling/tool-calls.go\",\n    \"integration_tests/test_observability_streaming.py\",\n    \"unit_tests/test_openai_compat_header_mapping.go\",\n    \"docs/api/observability.md\",\n    \"deploy/canary/observability-flag.yaml\",\n    \"sdk-ts/observability/parse_stream_prefix.ts\",\n    \"sdk-python/observability/stream_prefix.py\"\n  ],\n  \"review_comments\": [\n    \"Miguel Alvarez: Can we avoid increasing tag cardinality for metrics?
